data.narrative:
Shift5 is a Series C-stage defense and security company that has raised $180.5M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of 10 comparable companies—2 public and 8 private—within the Defense & Security sector at similar or proximate stages, including Castelion, Stark Defence, Neros, Anduril Industries, and Helsing.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses total capital raised ($180M) as a proxy for current value, applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement, yielding $307M. The peer-median method isolates 3 same-sector, same-stage comparables with a median valuation of $4.0B, ranging from $2.5B (Neros) to $13.0B (Castelion). This wider dispersion reflects heterogeneity in business model maturity and revenue within the cohort.

The triangulated analysis produces a range of $261M to $4.6B, with a median of $2.2B across both methods. The substantial gap between stage-progression and peer-median estimates reflects uncertainty around whether Shift5's commercial traction and defensibility align with the higher-valued peers or represent an earlier inflection point. Resolution of this range hinges on revenue scale, customer concentration, and gross margins relative to the peer set. The peer-median method carries greater weight given direct sector comparability, though the wide peer dispersion ($2.5B–$13.0B) indicates material uncertainty in appropriate comparables.
